chunks: Al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام was asked about a woman who dies among men with whom there is no mahram present: should they perform ghusl for her while her clothes are upon her?
So he said: "Then that would impose hardship upon them; rather, they should wash only her hands."

key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: the woman in question who has died
key_terms.ذُو مَحْرَمٍ: a male relative within the prohibited degrees of marriage
key_terms.يُدْخَلَ: it would impose or bring difficulty
key_terms.يُغَسِّلُونَهَا: they perform the ritual washing of the deceased upon her

ai.seo_question: What should be done if a woman dies among men who are not her mahrams?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling concerning the handling of a deceased woman when only unrelated men are present. It indicates that full ghusl is not to be carried out by them in such a circumstance, and instead only her hands are to be washed.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.426 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) was asked about a woman who passes away among a group of men with no male relative (mahram) present. Should they wash her while She remains clothed?
Imam (as) replied: "If they do that, it will be burdensome for them. Rather, they should wash only her hands."
